findings.reason: the followup is the plan's next-step carrier, so as written it dispatches a done section and leaves the new one unbuilt.
findings.text: `f-hpdw-010` is the only open followup and its prompt `/reckon-build history-persists-as-detail-washes-out §21` names a section now declared done, its body says "Review and build §21 to §27; §26 waits on §21 to §25", and the plan's own `plan-section-depends-on` now makes §26 wait on §21–§25 plus §28, so the next dispatch is pointed at landed work and §28 is never invoked

findings.reason: the node must invent the discriminator, and either invention (content match or a second marker) changes which repositories stay guarded.
findings.text: s28 requires that "a repository holding only the static-site `index.json` that `reckon build` writes ... is not recognised as crew-managed" and in the same breath that "§25's test still passes", but §25's landed `tests/test_guards_hold_without_a_tracked_ledger.py::_project_repo` builds a repository whose only marker is `index.json` containing `{}` and asserts both guards and `cli_entry._crew_state_exists` recognise it, so the two clauses are jointly satisfiable only if the discriminator is the `index.json` content (the baked envelope's `doc`/`data`/`inventory` keys) rather than its presence, which s28 never states

findings.reason: the recognition arm names a mechanism the guarded detector deliberately avoided, so a node would either widen the guard's read scope silently or ship an untestable clause.
findings.text: s28's other arm, "A repository with a run store and no tracked `crew.json` is still recognised", makes a signal the detector cannot hold: the store is `<config-home>/crew/run_store.db`, one shared database across projects (`reckon/run_store.py:182`), and `native_agent_guard.crew_managed_projects` documents and implements repository-local-only detection under `docs/state/*` (both guards' `PROJECT_STATE_MARKERS` and `cli_entry._CREW_STATE_MARKERS` read that directory), with §25's own landed test stating "The run ledger lives in the crew store outside every repository" — so the arm either requires the guard to start reading the shared home store on every spawn or is not constructible as a repository state at all

findings.reason: a named deliverable with no measure is the one that ships unproven, and the section's stated failure mode is exactly that script reporting zero.
findings.text: s24's Why names two readers to restate (velocity and "the review-cycle figure script", committed at `docs/figures/plan-review-cycles/measure_review_cycles.py:333`) and its write paths list that script, but its done-when measures velocity alone, so the node can satisfy every clause while the figure script still reports zero after the files leave git

findings.reason: the equality arm and the empty-store control already pin the required behaviour, so a reader resolves "or refuses" to a store that genuinely cannot answer and no node is sent down a wrong path.
findings.text: s24's first clause allows velocity to "answer from the store or refuse naming the store", while its second clause requires the figures to equal the ledger's over a nonzero population and its control requires an empty store to fail the comparison, so refusal is admitted by one sentence and excluded by the next two
